reading.body:
August Pfluger's AI record is legislative and financial at once: five sponsored or cosponsored AI bills and four recorded votes, alongside four PAC contributions from Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft totaling $6,000.

The pattern is that the money and the legislation come from the same small set of firms. Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft are the only donors listed, and the bills cover AI research, secure networks, China threat assessment, generative AI terrorism risk, and deepfake exploitation. The contributions are modest by federal standards, between $1,000 and $2,000 each, and they arrive across 2025 and 2026 rather than clustering around any single vote.

For AI specifically, this is the legislative layer of the compute buildout. Bills on secure networks and AI research sit upstream of the data centers and power contracts that determine how fast models can be trained and served. The donor list is the same set of companies whose capital expenditure now runs through grid interconnection queues. Money at this scale does not buy a vote, and the data does not claim it does.

What the data does not cover is decisive. It holds no votes against these bills, no committee assignments, no district-level data on data centers or power in Texas, and no contributions from utilities, grid operators, or equipment makers. It cannot show whether any contribution preceded, followed, or influenced any bill. It is a dated list of 14 events, and it should be read as one.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for August Pfluger: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 14 events, and 1 news stories that name them.
